subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should authenticated hooks be allowed to opt into re-entering an existing stored session through an explicit persistent mode under the current session-key prefix policy?
rationale: The implementation is concrete and proof-backed, but choosing whether webhook callers may attach to stored conversation state defines a security and context-isolation boundary that automation cannot approve.

options.title: Allow explicit persistent mode
options.body: Accept persistent reuse only when explicitly requested, preserve isolated as the default, and enforce the existing hook-auth and allowed-session-prefix checks.

options.title: Keep hooks always isolated
options.body: Reject stored-session attachment, close the linked pull request, and update webhook documentation so stable keys are not described as providing transcript continuity.

recommendation.title: Allow explicit persistent mode
recommendation.body: Accept persistent reuse only when explicitly requested, preserve isolated as the default, and enforce the existing hook-auth and allowed-session-prefix checks.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter already reviewed this exact issue and articulated the explicit opt-in design and security constraints requiring confirmation.
